title: VelclawDeploy
summary: Use the canonical deployment surface to prepare releases, inspect deployment evidence, and keep delivery state auditable.

sections.heading: Canonical deployment surface
body: The /deploy route is the canonical Velclaw Deploy control plane. It provides a first-party deployment surface without introducing a competing orchestration system.
Deployment is connected to the existing repository and delivery workflow so preparation, execution, and evidence remain in the same project context.

sections.heading: Deployment flow
body: A practical delivery sequence is: select the project and target, prepare the release, execute the provider adapter, collect deployment evidence, then verify runtime health.
Autoship and provider adapters can participate in delivery, while VelclawDeploy remains the product-facing control surface.

sections.heading: What to verify
bullets: Preview or production URL when supplied by the provider
Runtime health and critical route checks
Logs or failure evidence when a rollout does not complete

sections.heading: Failure handling
body: A failed deployment should remain visible as a failed delivery state. Do not silently convert a failed provider operation into a successful UI state.
Self-hosted Kubernetes delivery can use rollout checks and an undo path when the configured workflow supports it; provider-specific rollback behavior remains provider dependent.
